questions.question: Which number is the biggest: 42, 37, 24, or 73?
questions.explain: Look at the tens digit first: 7 tens beats 4 tens, so 73 is the biggest. The trap is comparing only the ones digits and picking 37.

questions.question: On the number line, which is the biggest: 58, 49, 95, or 94?
questions.explain: Check the tens digit first: 9 tens beats 5 tens and 4 tens, so 95 is the biggest. Don't just compare the ones digits.

questions.question: On the number line, put 23, 32, and 35 in order from smallest to biggest. Which is right?
questions.explain: Check the tens digits first: 2, then 3, then 3. Within the 30s, 32 comes before 35, so the order is 23, 32, 35.

questions.question: On the number line, which is bigger: 63 or 36?
questions.explain: Compare the tens digit: 6 is bigger than 3, so 63 is bigger. 36 is just 63 with the digits flipped, but they are different numbers.

questions.question: Maya has 47 stickers. Sam has 74 stickers. Who has more stickers?
questions.explain: Look at the tens: 7 tens beats 4 tens, so Sam has more stickers. Don't just compare the ones digits.

questions.question: A shop has Box A with 28 juice boxes and Box B with 82 juice boxes. Which box has more?
questions.explain: Check the tens digit: 8 tens beats 2 tens, so Box B has more. Comparing only the ones digits gives the wrong answer.

questions.question: Lily found 35 shells at the beach. Tom found 53 shells. Who found fewer shells?
questions.explain: Compare the tens first: 3 tens is less than 5 tens, so Lily found fewer. The ones digits can trick you.

questions.question: Anna has 47 marbles. She gives 3 to Ben. Ben had 35 marbles. Who has more now?
questions.explain: First, 47 minus 3 is 44. Then compare 44 and 38: 4 tens beats 3 tens, so Anna has more. Don't just look at the ones digits 4 and 8.

questions.question: A child writes: 62 is less than 26. What went wrong?
options: The child compared only the ones.
The child swapped the two digits.
The child added the two numbers.
The child wrote a whole new number.
questions.explain: The child looked at the ones digits: 2 is less than 6, so they wrote 62 is less than 26. You must compare the tens digit first.

questions.question: A teacher asks the class to put 43, 34, and 56 in order from smallest to biggest. Which child is right?
questions.explain: Check the tens digits: 3, then 4, then 5. So 34 comes first, then 43, then 56. Don't go from biggest to smallest.

questions.question: A number is bigger than 63 and smaller than 67. Which number fits?
questions.explain: The number must start with 6 and be between 63 and 67, so 65 fits. 36 is just 63 with the digits flipped.

questions.question: Three classes collected bottles for the school drive. Room A brought 27, Room B brought 72, and Room C brought 39. Put the numbers from smallest to biggest.
questions.explain: Compare the tens first: 2 tens, then 3 tens, then 7 tens, so 27, 39, 72. Smallest to biggest means the smallest number comes first.

questions.question: Leo is putting two bus numbers in order. He has 46 and 64 and does not know which one is bigger. What is the best way to start?
options: Compare the tens first: 6 tens beats 4 tens.
Swap the digits, then compare the two numbers.
Compare the ones first: 6 ones beats 4 ones.
Pick the number that you say first out loud.
questions.explain: Tens are worth more than ones, so check the tens digit first. 64 has 6 tens and 46 has only 4 tens, so 64 is bigger.

questions.question: Ben collected cans for the food bank. He collected 5 tens and 2 ones. Which number of cans is more than Ben's?
questions.explain: 5 tens and 2 ones is 52, so look for more than 52 by checking the tens first. Only 58 has more; 49 has a big ones digit but just 4 tens.

questions.question: Four friends picked apples at a farm near Abbotsford. Ava picked 61, Ben picked 16, Cleo picked 93, and Dan picked 48. Who picked the fewest apples?
questions.explain: Check the tens first: 16 has only 1 ten, so Ben picked the fewest. A big ones digit does not make a number big.
